items.title: 'My ears were ringing': Fierce storm leaves trail of damage in Damansara Damai
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A resident of Pangsapuri Saujana in Damansara Damai was left shaken after a storm struck the area yesterday, damaging his car when a tree branch fell on it. Pangsapuri Suria resident Rafizan Ramli, 40, said the large trees in the densely populated residential area had not been properly maintained. Rafizan said fallen trees also blocked several major roads, causing severe traffic congestion.

items.title: Sabah to act on Mengalum Island tourist death if safety breaches found
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government will take necessary action if any regulatory or safety violations are established following an investigation into the death of a Chinese tourist at Mengalum Island on Sept 23. State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the ministry would coordinate with relevant agencies to verify the compliance status of the operator, vessel, tourism activities and facilities involved in the incident. Jafry said the verification would cover whether the relevant licences and approvals were valid, required safety procedures had been followed, adequate safety equipment was available, safety briefings had been provided, sufficient supervision was in place and emergency response procedures had been observed.

items.title: Goh Sze Fei‑Nur Izzuddin storm into quarterfinals as Pearly Tan‑Thinaah sparkle with straight‑set wins
items.summary: NAGOYA, Sept 26 — Malaysia’s national professional men’s doubles pair, Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, are one step away from securing a medal at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games after advancing to the quarterfinals following a straight-set victory over Japan’s Yugo Kobayashi-Takuro Hoki today. During the match held at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium, the national pair faced no major issues in claiming a 21-19, 21-16 straight-set win. Meanwhile, another national men’s doubles pair, Aaron Chia and Tee Kai Wun, fell short of reaching the quarterfinals of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after bowing out to South Korea’s world number one pair, Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, in straight sets of 21-19, 21-16.

items.title: 'Malays are not immigrants', says academic
items.summary: MELAKA: Malays should not be labelled immigrants in the Malay Archipelago, particularly in Tanah Melayu, as their history is closely linked to the centuries-old merantau tradition, said International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation, International Islamic University Malaysia (ISTAC-IIUM) director Prof Datuk Dr Ahmad Murad Merican. He said the movement of Malay communities between regions in the Malay Archipelago should be understood as part of the merantau tradition, rather than migration viewed solely through the lens of modern political borders. She said Tanah Melayu was referred to in the Constitution through two main terms, namely the 'States of Malaya' (Negeri-negeri Tanah Melayu) and the 'Malay Peninsula' (Semenanjung Tanah Melayu).

items.title: As heavy rain and flooding continue in Bangkok, Malaysians urged to stay vigilant
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 26 — Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to exercise caution and remain vigilant as persistent heavy rain and flooding continue to disrupt roads and daily activities across the Thai capital, with all 50 districts declared disaster zones. In an advisory issued Saturday, the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok urged Malaysians residing in or travelling to the city to keep abreast of the latest weather, road, and traffic conditions and plan their journeys in advance. It said the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) provides an online Road Flood Monitoring System that allows the public to check road conditions and water levels at monitoring points across the capital.

items.title: 'Stop glorifying bullying': Asyraf Wajdi urges media ban following hostel student death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All forms of drama and films depicting bullying that could risk triggering a "copycat" culture among youths should be stopped, said Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. He said such content could encourage youths to imitate the behaviour and portray themselves as kapla, taiko or otai. "Stop all forms of drama or films that indirectly promote bullying in the name of 'lessons', which eventually lead to 'copycat' behaviour among youths who portray themselves as kapla, taiko, otai and others," he said in a statement on Facebook today.

items.title: Fama readies warehouses nationwide with buffer stocks as El Niño threat rises
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 26 — The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) has taken proactive steps to safeguard the nation’s food supply by establishing a special committee two months ago to prepare for the possible impact of El Nino. Its chairman, Abang Ahmad Kerdee Abang Masagus, said the move reflected Fama’s early action to prepare for the phenomenon, including plans to procure and store agro-food products at Fama warehouses nationwide. “At Fama, we established a committee two months ago.

items.title: Flash floods briefly hit UM campus amid new students' registration [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya (UM) was briefly affected by flash floods following heavy rain in the capital this afternoon. The incident occurred as new undergraduate students began reporting for residential college registration today. #NSTnation Universiti Malaya (UM) was briefly affected by flash floods following heavy rain in the capital this afternoon.

items.title: #NSTViral: 'If it's not enough, come and see me'
items.summary: According to a Threads post by user @kalaivanirajagopal, the boy would often spend recess sitting behind the computer lab, sometimes without anything to eat. That changed when the canteen worker, known as Kak Zira, noticed him and began giving him free food every day. "If it's not enough, come and see me," Kak Zira told him.

items.title: 280 Titiwangsa students receive RM1,000 education aid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 280 tertiary students from the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency have received RM1,000 each in financial assistance to help meet their educational needs. The assistance was presented by Titiwangsa member of parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today. Johari, who is also Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, said the annual assistance was aimed at helping students from low-income families pursue higher education.

items.title: Heavy rain triggers flash floods, traffic chaos in KL, Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor were hit by flash floods and traffic disruptions following heavy rain and thunderstorms this afternoon. The Kuala Lumpur Command & Control Centre (KLCCC) reported several traffic disruptions linked to the heavy rain. At 4.08pm, heavy rain around Kuala Lumpur resulted in congestion along Jalan Damansara and Jalan Kinabalu.

items.title: Karnival Jom Heboh gives Sarawak entrepreneurs platform to reach wider market
items.summary: MIRI: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) is more than an entertainment event, providing entrepreneurs with an opportunity to showcase their products to thousands of visitors, said Sarawak Deputy Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister Datuk Dr Ripin Lamat. He said the participation of entrepreneurs and agencies through exhibition booths at KJH allowed them to promote their products, build networks and expand their businesses. "We can see various booths by entrepreneurs and agencies taking part in the exhibition.

items.title: Nepal missing Malaysians cannot be presumed dead after a month: Penang mufti
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians missing in Nepal following landslides and floods along the Nepal-Tibet border cannot automatically be presumed dead simply because they have remained uncontactable for a month, said Penang Mufti Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Sukki Othman. He said under Islamic law, they fell under the category of al-mafqud — people who have gone missing, are out of contact and whose status as alive or dead cannot be established with certainty. Sukki said the missing Malaysians could not be categorised as deceased because Islamic law takes a cautious approach in matters involving life, marriage, inheritance and a person's rights.

items.title: Storm clouds gather: MetMalaysia issues urgent alert for Kuala Lumpur and 12 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 8pm today. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar and Manjung in Perak; Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Machang, Tanah Merah and Jeli in Kelantan. Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pulau Tioman, Temerloh, Jerantut and Kuantan in Pahang; Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling and Klang in Selangor; Kuala Pilah, Tampin, Rembau and Jempol in Negeri Sembilan; and Mersing in Johor.

items.title: Madani Mart’s master licensing push could fuel 300 outlets, says Fuziah
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 26 — Madani Mart is opening master licensing applications to companies, investors, and strategic partners with financial and operational capabilities to accelerate its retail network expansion nationwide. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said each party appointed by Yayasan Madani will have the opportunity to develop and operate up to 100 Madani Mart branches, subject to set terms and standards. She said expansion through this model will begin after Yayasan Madani ensures the supply chain and pricing for about 5,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs) offered by Madani Mart remain stable.

items.title: Families of missing Malaysians in Nepal to meet Wisma Putra officials tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following the Aug 26 glacial flash floods in Nepal will meet Wisma Putra officials tomorrow, seeking answers over the search for their loved ones. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families appreciated the government's efforts, including the deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) and diplomatic engagement led by Wisma Putra, but wanted greater clarity over developments on the China-Tibet side as well. The Nepalese authorities will continue the search, verification and identification efforts while Malaysia maintained diplomatic engagement with the relevant authorities.

items.title: 'Fly faster': AirAsia pilot beats drone delay, unaware of passenger's desperate viral plea
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An AirAsia pilot unknowingly helped fulfil a passenger's desperate hope that her sister would make it back in time to bid their late grandmother a final farewell. Koh Yew Weng, 37, better known as Eric, was piloting flight AK5135 from Kota Kinabalu to Kuala Lumpur at 6am on Tuesday when a woman posted a plea on social media asking the captain to fly faster so her sister could attend the funeral before the burial. Eric only discovered the post after landing back in Kota Kinabalu later that day.

items.title: RM18.23mil hostel complex boosts SMK Majakir capacity to 300 students
items.summary: PAPAR: A new RM18.23 million hostel complex at SMK Majakir here has been completed, increasing the school's accommodation capacity from 160 to 300 students. "The old hostel could only accommodate 160 students, comprising 80 boys and 80 girls. The new complex comprises two two-storey hostel blocks, warden houses, dormitories for students with disabilities, common rooms, isolation rooms, warden offices and reception rooms.

items.title: Joachim: PBS to remain with GRS, strengthen multiracial identity
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) will continue working with Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) while strengthening the party as a modern, multiracial and integrity-driven political entity, said its president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam. He said the new PBS leadership would be guided by three main pillars — unity, stability and integrity — in line with the theme of the 41st PBS Congress held today. PBS belongs to everyone who believes in the struggle for Sabah," he said.

items.title: Van impaled by guardrail in Kuching crash, passenger injured
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 26 — A passenger van was impaled by a roadside guardrail after crashing at a traffic light junction in Bandar Baru Samariang this morning. See Hua Daily News reported that the incident occurred at about 7am today. The van was carrying one female passenger at the time.

items.title: Anwar questions Opposition priorities: ‘No salary, they’re angry; those who steal, they don’t mention’
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned the federal Opposition’s priorities, taking a swipe at its MPs for scrutinising his refusal to draw a prime ministerial salary while, he said, saying little about those who “ sakau ”, or steal, large sums of money. Anwar recalled being questioned by Opposition MPs in Parliament over how he could support himself without taking his salary as prime minister. Anwar said the government also provides the vehicle he uses, accommodation at the prime minister’s official residence, Seri Perdana, and flights.

items.title: PBS to reinforce unity and integrity while remaining in GRS, says president
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam wants the party to be strengthened as a modern, multiracial and integrity-driven entity that remains relevant, while reaffirming its commitment to continue working with Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS). He said the direction of the new PBS leadership would be based on three main pillars — unity, stability and integrity — in line with the theme of the 41st PBS Congress held today, ‘Unity, Stability, Integrity’. He said the struggle concerning the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) was not yet over and PBS would continue to play an active role in defending Sabah’s rights and interests.

items.title: Damai Perdana residents anxious over uncertain return home
items.summary: CHERAS: Residents of Damai Perdana affected by a recent landslide are growing anxious over the lack of a clear timeline for when they can safely return home. Currently staying at the Taman Desa Baiduri multipurpose hall temporary relief centre, they said they had been told the evacuation would last a week, but had received no firm updates on the safety of their homes or the progress of slope repairs. S. Sossilan, 69, said the uncertainty had made it difficult for him and his wife to plan their daily routines.

items.title: Kuala Pilah Form Two student death: Cause still undetermined after post-mortem, police question 21
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A post-mortem has failed to establish the cause of death of a 14-year-old boy whose death is being investigated following allegations of bullying at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, with police awaiting the results of further tests. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the examination was carried out at the Forensic Medicine Department of Tuanku Jaafar Hospital in Seremban from 10.30am today, Harian Metro reported. He said police had so far recorded statements from 21 people, including students, teachers and the boy’s parents, as part of the investigation.

items.title: Malaysia's handicraft industry records RM240mil in sales as of July
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's handicraft industry recorded RM240.3 million in sales as of July, Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said. He said RM230.3 million, or 96 per cent, of the total came from the domestic market, while RM10 million, or 4 per cent, was generated from international markets. On MICF 2026, Chiew said the event played a strategic role in connecting local entrepreneurs with international buyers, markets and industry partners.

items.title: Sabah boosts efforts to attract Chinese tourists ahead of Visit Sabah 2027
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is stepping up efforts to attract more Chinese tourists ahead of Visit Sabah 2027, Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said. "China remains an important tourism market for Sabah. Jafry said Chongqing Airlines operated three direct flights a week to Sabah, while more flights between Sabah and Shanghai would be available by year-end as China Eastern Airlines and Spring Airlines planned to increase their flight schedules.

items.title: Sabah must move up value chain, produce high-value finished products: Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah must move towards producing and exporting high-value finished products to maximise returns from its agro-food sector, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. "We need to shift towards producing downstream products with high added value. Hajiji said strengthening downstream activities would also create employment opportunities, particularly for local youths.

items.title: Police await further tests to determine cause of student's death
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The cause of death of a 14-year-old boy allegedly bullied at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah remains undetermined following a post-mortem. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the post-mortem on Muhammad Idlan Fareeq Shahril was conducted at the Forensic Medicine Department of Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital (HTJ) here, beginning at 10.30am today. "The post-mortem, conducted by HTJ forensic pathology specialist Dr Akma Nurain Fairuz Mahamad Arif, was completed at 3pm today.

items.title: Govt to announce firm measures to ensure fair wages in Budget 2027, says Anwar
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was currently at the final stage of preparing the budget and would formulate more concerted efforts to ensure that wage increases were commensurate with graduates’ qualifications. Take South Korea, for example, particularly where productivity is high, and wages have also increased accordingly. Asked about management issues and weaknesses at UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar said the matter needed to be studied before taking any action.

items.title: Anwar says he has not received Loke’s resignation letter
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has yet to receive Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s resignation letter. Loke offered to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on September 19 in response to the conditional pardon granted to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. RoS issued the suspension order, effective September 23, covering all PN activities.

items.title: ‘Not a zero-sum game’: Anwar says he wants to help Malays, but not by denying others’ rights
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he wants to help Malays in the country, while stressing that this should not come at the expense of the rights of others because it is not a “zero-sum game”. “But I ‘ tidak senang ’ (dislike) any views that insult others, that belittle others’ roles or deny the rights of others. Just before making the remarks, Anwar invited UiTM alumni to select seven to 10 representatives to evaluate programmes under Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM itself, and propose improvements.

items.title: Abang Johari warns against race-based politics in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg has warned political parties against playing on emotions or adopting race-based policies in the new era. He said such an approach could leave certain communities excluded from the state's overall development. "We must remain vigilant and ensure Sarawak moves forward towards 2030 with policies that encompass all races," he said.

items.title: Khaled Nordin: Malaysia to reinforce defence, especially in Sabah, amid South China Sea tensions
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Malaysia needs to strengthen its national defence, particularly in Sabah, as a precaution in the event of a clash between major powers in the South China Sea. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia’s main concern was the possibility of a conflict or unexpected incident in the area that could have spillover effects on the country, particularly Sabah. “Every country has its own right to strengthen its national defence.

items.title: RM1.15m gone: Female farmer falls for love scam, fake gold investment
items.summary: KUANTAN: A farmer lost over RM1.15 million after falling victim to a love scam syndicate. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 50-year-old woman, befriended an individual named Siew Gui Lim @ Jason via WhatsApp on July 17 before their relationship grew closer. "The suspect then posed as a cybersecurity consulting director and offered a gold investment, promising the victim profits.

items.title: Zahid: BN to hold separate talks with two coalitions next week
items.summary: AYER KEROH: BN will hold separate meetings with two political coalitions next week to discuss possible cooperation for the Melaka election, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. The BN chairman confirmed that the meetings would be held at the BN headquarters at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL). The meetings will be led by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, together with the top leaders of the two coalitions.

items.title: Anwar wants pondok education elevated, youths exposed to Islamic knowledge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants pondok education to be elevated and younger generations to be exposed to the wealth of Islamic knowledge. He said this would ensure that progress brought greater good when guided by faith, good character and a sense of responsibility towards others. Anwar said the history of the nation could not be separated from pondok schools and pesantren, which preserved faith, safeguarded knowledge and educated generations to maintain their identity during colonial rule.

items.title: Anwar reaffirms commitment to Malays, Bumiputeras while protecting others' rights
items.summary: Anwar said the Bumiputera agenda could be strengthened while upholding social justice and respecting the rights and interests of non-Malays. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he had never supported views that insulted other communities, belittled their contributions or denied their rights. Anwar said the government would continue to prioritise Bumiputera development through policies and agencies aimed at strengthening economic, social and educational opportunities.

items.title: Woman loses RM1.15m after falling for love scam syndicate in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 26 — A farmer and agricultural product trader lost more than RM1.15 million after falling victim to a love scam syndicate. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 50-year-old woman, befriended an individual known as Siew Gui Lim @ Jason via WhatsApp on July 17 before their relationship grew closer. “The suspect then posed as a cybersecurity consulting director and offered a gold investment, promising the victim profits.

items.title: Anwar signals fairer bonus distribution in 2027 Budget
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was reviewing how bonuses are distributed between chief executives and lower-paid workers. Anwar said he had encountered situations where chief executive officers (CEOs) received bonuses equivalent to eight months' salary while workers received only two months. Anwar said if workers were given a three-month bonus, CEOs should also receive a bonus equivalent to three months.

items.title: Anwar says company losses are not a crime — fraud, abuse and ‘sakau’ are another matter
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Companies should not be penalised simply because they make losses, but action should be taken where there is fraud, abuse of power or “ sakau ”, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Speaking after addressing issues including the scrutiny of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Anwar said companies could go through periods of losses as well as profits, and that losses alone should not be grounds for punishment. Turning to UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar cautioned against passing judgment before its position had been properly examined.

items.title: Anwar approves RM2.5mil to upgrade UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub campus
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved RM2.5 million to upgrade the newly renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman campus in Petaling Jaya. The allocation was announced by Anwar during the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM here, following his declaration that the UiTM Jalan Othman campus would be renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said UiTM's operating and development allocation had increased significantly under the Madani government.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across much of Malaysia until this evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across the country, except Sarawak, until 5pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Yan, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they comprise Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak. In Pahang, the areas involved are Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor and Klang.

items.title: Mindef launches national defence literacy drive to prepare public for new security threats
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) today launched the National Defence Literacy Programme to boost the public’s awareness, knowledge and understanding of national defence, security and sovereignty. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a shifting security threat landscape demands a deeper understanding of national defence, and a recognition of the role Malaysians can play in safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty. “This is where what we call defence literacy comes in.

items.title: Anwar: UiTM Jalan Othman Campus renamed in honour of Arshad Ayub, architect of institution’s early growth
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Jalan Othman Campus in Petaling Jaya has been renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman Campus in recognition of the late educationist’s contributions to the development of the institution. Anwar said the renaming was a tribute to Arshad’s legacy, having played a key role in the development of the Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM) into UiTM, while also being known for his firm emphasis on educational quality, good governance and expanding educational opportunities for Bumiputera students. Anwar said Arshad had also maintained a strong commitment to governance and institutional integrity, rather than using Malay institutions or agencies for personal gain or allowing them to be undermined by misconduct.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah: Removing 30pc Bumiputera equity rule for private education will not weaken empowerment agenda
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Sept 26 — The removal of the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for private education institutions (IPS) will not undermine the government’s agenda to empower the community, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. At the event, the minister was also presented with the RIYI 2026 closing summary report, which highlighted a gap between students’ expectations and employers’ assessments of graduates’ workplace readiness. Meanwhile, 62 per cent of students said they felt adequately prepared by their universities, while only 32.3 per cent of employers agreed that local universities sufficiently prepared graduates for workplace realities.

items.title: Sarawak to set up authority to manage and develop lakes, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 26 — Sarawak will establish an authority to oversee, manage and develop the state’s lake areas in a comprehensive manner. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the initiative is part of the state’s development plans for the next five years. Meanwhile, he said the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak (CENTEXS) would establish a Flying School Academy in Betong to support the state’s efforts to advance modern agriculture through drone technology.

items.title: Kuskop channels nearly RM10b to 270,000 entrepreneurs as of August, seeks bigger Budget 2027 allocation, says minister
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 26 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development (Kuskop) has channelled nearly RM10 billion through various support and financing programmes under the ‘Power Up 10K’ initiative to about 270,000 entrepreneurs nationwide as of the end of August. “The RM10 billion is part of the RM15 billion target to be channelled to the MSME and cooperative sectors this year. Sim noted that financing support for the MSME sector had been increased to RM60 billion this year from RM50 billion previously.

items.title: Over 86pc of Perlis patients seen within an hour under digital medical record pilot, says Fahmi
items.summary: PADANG BESAR, Sept 26 — The pilot Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system implemented under the National Digital Health Ecosystem and Connectivity Driver (Persada) initiative at health facilities in Perlis has had a positive impact on patient waiting times, said Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Perlis Health director Dr Ghazali Chik. Fahmi said doctors no longer had to wait for patients’ medical records to be retrieved manually, as all relevant information could be accessed through the system.

items.title: Nancy: Don’t just add seats — decide Sabah-Sarawak representation formula first
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 26 — Putrajaya must first work out the one-third formula for Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat before adding any parliamentary seats. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said she and several Sarawak leaders, including in Cabinet, have raised the issue, but the focus had previously been more on state assembly seats. Previously, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed in principle to increase the ratio of Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the regions’ position in the formation of Malaysia through the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).

items.title: Zahid: BN to hold separate talks with two groups next week over Melaka state election cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will hold separate talks with two different groups next week as it weighs possible political partnerships ahead of the Melaka state election, chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today. According to Sinar Harian , he said BN headquarters had arranged the meetings for different dates and times. Two different groups,” he said.

items.title: ‘Digitalisation should not create a divide’: Gobind urges inclusive tech push
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The national digital transformation agenda must be implemented inclusively and cannot solely benefit those with access to technology. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the digitalisation process must also ensure that the digitally less literate, elderly, low-income groups and small entrepreneurs can enjoy the same benefits. Gobind, who is also the Damansara Member of Parliament, said the national digitalisation agenda was not solely about technology, but about people.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh suggests standardising routes to reduce road closures for KL running events
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Running event organisers in the capital are being told to standardise their routes with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to curb disruptions to the city with endless road closures. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said one fix worth considering is to set standard routes based on running distances, and make organisers stick to them. Hannah said the coordination is crucial because road users need to know in advance which routes are affected so they can plan their journeys.

items.title: PAS logo an option for Perikatan in Melaka election if RoS suspension remains, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) may contest the Melaka state election under the PAS logo if the coalition’s suspension by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) remains in force, secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today. According to Harian Metro , Takiyuddin said the choice of logo was not a major issue for the coalition, which would decide its approach according to the circumstances ahead of the election. He said PAS had no difficulty contesting under its own logo, while Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia could also contest using its own symbol.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt to cover postal delivery costs for medicines from Oct 1 under MCMC-MOH initiative
items.summary: PADANG BESAR, Sept 26 — The Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), will help the Health Ministry (MoH) provide free postal delivery of medicines to patients who opt for the service from October 1. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative would be implemented nationwide with an allocation of about RM5 million. Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Perlis Health director Dr Ghazali Chik.

items.title: Malaysia says pandemic prevention and preparedness must be shared global responsibility, Tok Mat tells UN
items.summary: No nation can secure its health in isolation,” said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan in Malaysia’s statement at the High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response here yesterday. Malaysia has translated this lesson into action, Mohamad shared at the meeting. Taking public health seriously, Mohamad said Malaysia is implementing the ‘One Health’ approach to mitigate microbiological threats in food, water and the environment.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan police chief: 16-year-old remanded six days over murder probe into Kuala Pilah Form Two student’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 16-year-old Form Four student detained in connection with the murder investigation into the death of a Form Two student at a Kuala Pilah school has been remanded for six days, until October 1. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the remand application was made at the Seremban Magistrates’ Court today. Police had earlier said the student was detained to assist investigations after the death was classified as murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
